description: Follow-up to question-citations-2026-08-04.json after a three-model adversarial review (Grok / GPT-5.6 / Gemini). Two classes of fix. (1) CURRENCY: regs 149 and 213 were both amended by GNR.846 of 31 Oct 2014, which post-dates the consolidated-to-GNR.209-of-2012 copy the first pass read. Reg 149 was substituted WHOLESALE — the proviso relied on survives verbatim but the excluded-vehicle list changed, so the first pass quoted superseded wording. Reg 213 gained an infant definition (1)(c) and a new (6A) infant restraint duty; subregs (4) and (11) as cited are untouched. Both citations now name the amendment and the quotes are re-read from it. This is the trap recorded in resources/README.md and CLAUDE.md — 'the 2000 original is not the law in force' — reaching one consolidation further forward than expected. (2) FLAG THRESHOLD: the review's strongest process criticism was that composite keyed answers were backfilled with a citation rather than flagged, and it converged on items the first pass should have marked partial by its own standard. Seven more now carry NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER. No keyed answer is changed and no question is approved or verified by this file.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §3 §2.6 sample questions; NRTR 2000 reg 149 as substituted by GNR.846 of 31 Oct 2014

ops.why: CURRENCY FIX. Reg 149 was substituted in full by r. 41 of GNR.846 (GG 38142, 31 Oct 2014), after the 2012 consolidation the first pass read. The proviso relied on is unchanged — '(a) the emergency brake and parking brake may be one and the same brake' — but the opening now reads 'a motor vehicle, other than a motor cycle, motor tricycle or trailer', dropping 'motor quadrucycle', and (b)(iii) now reads 'a tractor or haulage tractor'. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: reg 149 establishes only that the parking brake may double as the emergency brake. It does NOT state that the service brake is the control for an emergency stop — that rests solely on manual §2.6 — and it does not support the learner explanation's claim that the handbrake is a fallback 'if the service brake fails'. Two reviewers flagged that prose as exceeding the regulation. The explanation also names 'regulation 149' at the learner, which constraint 10 forbids; fix when the prose is next touched.

set.source_citation: NRTR 2000 reg 213(4) and reg 213(11), as amended to GNR.846 of 31 Oct 2014

ops.why: CURRENCY FIX. Reg 213 was amended by r. 52 of GNR.846 (2014), which added the definition '(c) an infant is a person below the age of three years' to subreg (1) and inserted subreg (6A) requiring an appropriate child restraint for infants. Neither touches (4) or (11), so the quoted text stands: '(4) No adult shall occupy a seat in a motor vehicle operated on a public road which is fitted with a seatbelt unless such person wears such seatbelt' and '(11) The driver of a motor vehicle shall ensure that all persons travelling in such motor vehicle shall wear a seat belt'. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: the duty attaches to occupying a seat in a vehicle 'operated on a public road', which implies but does not state the keyed timing 'before the vehicle moves off'. Two reviewers flagged this as a timing gloss.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §3 §2.2 items 1 and 3; §2.6 sample questions

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: §2.6 ('Which control(s) is/are used to see what is to the rear and sides of the vehicle? 1 and 3') supports the MIRRORS only. The keyed answer's parenthetical 'and a direct look over your shoulder' appears in no source in resources/. Same gap as RR-041, where 'blind spot' is likewise absent.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §1 §6.49; NRTR 2000 reg 308(1)(b)

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: the two-second figure rests SOLELY on manual §6.49. Reg 308(1)(b) carries only the qualitative duty not to 'follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonable and prudent' and contains no number. This is the same statutory-vs-syllabus split already flagged on RR-054, and should be read the same way: the manual is evidence of syllabus scope, not of law in force.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §1 §6.27 and §6.49; NRTR 2000 reg 292

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: reg 292 prescribes the general speed limits and nothing more. It does not characterise them as ceilings for good conditions, and contains no weather-based reduction duty. That half of the keyed answer rests entirely on manual §6.49's adverse-conditions rule, which is itself written about following distance rather than speed.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §1 §6.49; §3 §2.6 sample questions (braking distance)

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: the keyed answer is a three-step causal chain and only two steps are sourced. 'Braking distance is longer' on a wet road comes from §3 §2.6; 'leave a bigger gap' from §1 §6.49. The first step — that tyres have LESS GRIP — is stated in neither, so the mechanism the question asks the learner to reason about is the unsourced part.

FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: §6.42 makes indicators compulsory 'each time when turning left or to the right and when changing lanes'. Treating an exit from a mini-circle as such a turn is an inference; no source in resources/ addresses signalling within or on leaving a traffic circle. The citation does firmly refute the keyed distractor that indicators are not used inside a circle.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §2 — Traffic lights, Action

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: 'Amber - Stop, except where it cannot be done safely' establishes that stopping is the default and carrying on the exception. It does not describe HOW to brake, so the keyed answer's 'firmly but under control' is unsourced wording — it comes from the scenario's premise rather than from the rule.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §3 §2.5 items 6 and 8

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: §2.5 establishes that an automatic has no clutch control and that its gear lever 'operates differently from a manual gear box system'. That it 'selects gears itself' is an inference from 'operates differently' and is not stated. The no-clutch half of the keyed answer is solid.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §3 §2.2 item 8; §2.6 sample questions

ops.why: FLAG ONLY — citation unchanged. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN VERIFIER: the sources establish that the clutch is used together with the gear lever to change gear (§2.6: 'In order to change a gear, you must use control/s … 6 and 8'). The keyed answer's mechanism — 'by disconnecting the engine from the wheels' — is not in the quoted text; the nearest is §1.3's motorcycle item, 'Which control is used to disengage the engine from the gearbox? — 2', which says gearbox rather than wheels.

set.source_citation: SA Learner Driver Manual §2 — Traffic lights, Action; §7.1 Stop line (RTM1)

ops.why: Narrowed. The first pass also cited '§3.1 Stop sign action', which is where the words 'behind the stop line' literally appear — but that is the STOP SIGN entry, and importing it to complete a TRAFFIC LIGHT proposition was flagged as a mismatched source. The claim stands without it: 'Red - Stop' gives the duty, and RTM1's own purpose gives the position — 'To indicate where you must bring your vehicle to a standstill'. RTM1 is the correct provision for where a stop line requires you to stop, whatever caused the stop.

review_record.reviewers: x-ai/grok-4.3, openai/gpt-5.6-luna, google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite — independent, same packet, same focus
review_record.consensus_no_finding: All three agreed that (a) none of the 7 declared-uncitable questions is citable from the Act, the regulations or the 2012 DoT manuals, and (b) no keyed answer is wrong as a matter of South African law. The first pass's uncitable list was not premature.
review_record.false_positive_recorded: Gemini raised its only HIGH against RR-053, asserting that NRTR reg 304 governs leaving a vehicle unattended and that the stopping prohibitions live in reg 305. This is refuted by the consolidated text: reg 304 IS 'Stopping of vehicles', and reg 304(h) is verbatim the cited rule — no stopping 'within nine metres of his or her approaching side of a pedestrian crossing demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs'. Reg 305 is 'Parking of vehicles'. The reviewer cited from recall and inverted the two. Recorded because it is precisely the failure mode constraint 9 exists to prevent, and it was produced BY a verification tool.
review_record.safety_note: GPT-5.6 raised a content-safety point on q-controls-5 (already uncitable, already queued for a decision): a red oil-pressure or brake warning lamp may require stopping immediately, so the keyed answer 'check before driving' could be unsafe as written. Worth resolving when that question is decided rather than treating it as a citation problem.
